props.title:
Eat Well.
Find food that ==fits your life==.
props.subtitle: A curated collection of restaurants with the details diners actually decide on.

slides.notes: Warm open. Eat Well exists because eating out with dietary needs shouldn't be a research project. One sentence, then move on.

props.title: Finding a place you can ==actually eat well== is harder than it should be.

left.label: Today
left.title: Stitch it together yourself
points: Search results, menus, and review sites — in separate tabs
Dietary needs buried in menus or old photos
The details that matter most are the hardest to verify

right.label: With Eat Well
right.title: One place to decide
points: Every option in one browsable collection
What you tap is where you meant to go

slides.notes: Anchor on the user's pain: they're not short of restaurants, they're short of trustworthy details. Pause on 'hardest to verify'.

props.label: What it does
props.title: One focused collection — {c:#4ade80}built to decide with{/c}, not to scroll through.
props.body: Eat Well gathers restaurants into a single browsable experience, with the details diners actually decide on — dietary fit, practical info, and a link straight through to the place itself.

slides.notes: Keep this concrete: a focused discovery experience, not another infinite feed. The point is less scrolling, more deciding.

props.caption: of restaurant links researched and verified one by one — not scraped blindly, so what you tap is where you meant to go.
props.foot: Every link in the collection was checked by hand.

slides.notes: This is the trust slide. The data work is the moat: each link was visited and verified, which is why nothing dead-ends.
